# Thesis: Persistent co-movement of volume and VWAP ranks marks crowded trades. (Alpha #50, adapted) Blended with low accruals, whose returns move against short-term price signals (the recipe that qualified A101_054_acc, IR .137).
# Source: Kakushadze, "101 Formulaic Alphas" (2016), https://arxiv.org/abs/1601.00991; Sloan, The Accounting Review 1996, https://www.jstor.org/stable/248290
# Repair: accrual partner 1.5x. Parent A101_050 Fast IR .072.
c = ts_corr_binary(cs_rank(volume), cs_rank(vwap_last_hour), 5)  # 5-day corr of volume rank and VWAP rank
r = cs_zscore(-ts_max(cs_rank(c), 5))  # the original signal, z-scored
k = cs_zscore(-cs_rank((ts_fill(net_income) - ts_fill(cash_from_operations))/ts_fill(total_assets)))  # low accruals: earnings backed by cash (Sloan 1996)
alpha = at_zero2nan(at_nan2zero(r) + 1.5*at_nan2zero(k))  # signal + accruals at 1.5x

# Thesis: A change in where the close sits within the day's range reverts. (Alpha #53, adapted) Blended with low accruals, whose returns move against short-term price signals (the recipe that qualified A101_054_acc, IR .137).
# Source: Kakushadze, "101 Formulaic Alphas" (2016), https://arxiv.org/abs/1601.00991; Sloan, The Accounting Review 1996, https://www.jstor.org/stable/248290
# Repair: accrual partner 1.5x. Parent A101_053 Fast IR .068.
pos = ((close - low) - (high - close))/(close - low + 0.001*close)  # close location within the day's range
r = cs_zscore(-delta(pos, 10))  # the original signal, z-scored
k = cs_zscore(-cs_rank((ts_fill(net_income) - ts_fill(cash_from_operations))/ts_fill(total_assets)))  # low accruals: earnings backed by cash (Sloan 1996)
alpha = at_zero2nan(at_nan2zero(r) + 1.5*at_nan2zero(k))  # signal + accruals at 1.5x

# Thesis: Days when volume growth and the open-to-close return move together tend to reverse. (Alpha #2, adapted) Blended with low accruals, whose returns move against short-term price signals (the recipe that qualified A101_054_acc, IR .137).
# Source: Kakushadze, "101 Formulaic Alphas" (2016), https://arxiv.org/abs/1601.00991; Sloan, The Accounting Review 1996, https://www.jstor.org/stable/248290
# Repair: accrual partner 1.5x. Parent A101_002 Fast IR .071.
dv = delta(at_signlog(volume), 2)  # 2-day change in log volume
oc = (close - open)/open  # open-to-close return
r = cs_zscore(-ts_corr_binary(cs_rank(dv), cs_rank(oc), 5))  # the original signal, z-scored
k = cs_zscore(-cs_rank((ts_fill(net_income) - ts_fill(cash_from_operations))/ts_fill(total_assets)))  # low accruals: earnings backed by cash (Sloan 1996)
alpha = at_zero2nan(at_nan2zero(r) + 1.5*at_nan2zero(k))  # signal + accruals at 1.5x

# Thesis: Persistent high-price/volume co-movement marks crowded moves that fade. (Alpha #15, adapted) Blended with low accruals, whose returns move against short-term price signals (the recipe that qualified A101_054_acc, IR .137).
# Source: Kakushadze, "101 Formulaic Alphas" (2016), https://arxiv.org/abs/1601.00991; Sloan, The Accounting Review 1996, https://www.jstor.org/stable/248290
# Repair: accrual partner 1.5x. Parent A101_015 Fast IR .073.
c = ts_corr_binary(cs_rank(high), cs_rank(volume), 3)  # 3-day corr of high-price rank and volume rank
r = cs_zscore(-ts_sum(cs_rank(c), 3))  # the original signal, z-scored
k = cs_zscore(-cs_rank((ts_fill(net_income) - ts_fill(cash_from_operations))/ts_fill(total_assets)))  # low accruals: earnings backed by cash (Sloan 1996)
alpha = at_zero2nan(at_nan2zero(r) + 1.5*at_nan2zero(k))  # signal + accruals at 1.5x

# Thesis: When volume and high-price both sit at local peaks together, the move is exhausted. (Alpha #26, adapted) Blended with low accruals, whose returns move against short-term price signals (the recipe that qualified A101_054_acc, IR .137).
# Source: Kakushadze, "101 Formulaic Alphas" (2016), https://arxiv.org/abs/1601.00991; Sloan, The Accounting Review 1996, https://www.jstor.org/stable/248290
# Repair: accrual partner 1.5x. Parent A101_026 Fast IR .073.
c = ts_corr_binary(ts_rank(volume, 5), ts_rank(high, 5), 5)  # corr of 5-day volume and high ranks
r = cs_zscore(-ts_max(c, 3))  # the original signal, z-scored
k = cs_zscore(-cs_rank((ts_fill(net_income) - ts_fill(cash_from_operations))/ts_fill(total_assets)))  # low accruals: earnings backed by cash (Sloan 1996)
alpha = at_zero2nan(at_nan2zero(r) + 1.5*at_nan2zero(k))  # signal + accruals at 1.5x

# Thesis: balance-sheet COMPOSITION composite. Each item scaled by total assets is a weak, slow characteristic (daily IR .03-.05 alone, turnover ~.03) whose sign held in-sample and out-of-sample (2017-21); combining several weakly related characteristics diversifies their noise, so the composite should carry a higher IR at the same tiny turnover (the IR/sqrt(turnover) route that qualified T_COMP7). Long firms funded by short-term operating liabilities with receivables/inventory-heavy, older (depreciated) asset bases; short goodwill-heavy (acquisitive) and long-term-debt-heavy firms.
# Source: Green, Hand & Zhang, "The Characteristics that Provide Independent Information about Average U.S. Monthly Stock Returns" (RFS 2017), https://doi.org/10.1093/rfs/hhx019; acquisitive firms underperform: Cooper, Gulen & Schill, "Asset Growth and the Cross-Section of Stock Returns" (JF 2008), https://doi.org/10.1111/j.1540-6261.2008.01370.x
# Note: signs were chosen from the first sweep run (field sweep batch 1), so this is partly data-selected; each sign was checked to hold out of sample (OOS1) before inclusion.
# Repair: 5 strongest legs + low-accruals leg (adds an independent slow premium). Parent SWC_BS9 IR .063, TVR .029, corr .477 (< .5), OOS1 .108; needs IR > .07.
# Source (accruals): Sloan, The Accounting Review 1996, https://www.jstor.org/stable/248290
ta = ts_fill(total_assets)  # total assets, carried forward between reports
cl = cs_zscore(cs_rank(ts_fill(current_liabilities)/ta))  # short-term operating liabilities per dollar of assets, ranked and z-scored
ar = cs_zscore(cs_rank(ts_fill(accounts_receivable_excluding_notes)/ta))  # receivables per dollar of assets, ranked and z-scored
gw = -cs_zscore(cs_rank(ts_fill(goodwill)/ta))  # goodwill from acquisitions (short) per dollar of assets, ranked and z-scored
ad = cs_zscore(cs_rank(ts_fill(accumulated_depreciation)/ta))  # accumulated depreciation (older asset base) per dollar of assets, ranked and z-scored
oc = cs_zscore(cs_rank(ts_fill(other_current_assets)/ta))  # other current assets per dollar of assets, ranked and z-scored
acc = cs_zscore(-cs_rank((ts_fill(net_income) - ts_fill(cash_from_operations))/ta))  # low accruals: earnings backed by cash (Sloan 1996)
alpha = at_zero2nan(at_nan2zero(cl) + at_nan2zero(ar) + at_nan2zero(gw) + at_nan2zero(ad) + at_nan2zero(oc) + at_nan2zero(acc))  # equal-weight composite; missing legs count as 0

# Thesis: balance-sheet COMPOSITION composite. Each item scaled by total assets is a weak, slow characteristic (daily IR .03-.05 alone, turnover ~.03) whose sign held in-sample and out-of-sample (2017-21); combining several weakly related characteristics diversifies their noise, so the composite should carry a higher IR at the same tiny turnover (the IR/sqrt(turnover) route that qualified T_COMP7). Long firms funded by short-term operating liabilities with receivables/inventory-heavy, older (depreciated) asset bases; short goodwill-heavy (acquisitive) and long-term-debt-heavy firms.
# Source: Green, Hand & Zhang, "The Characteristics that Provide Independent Information about Average U.S. Monthly Stock Returns" (RFS 2017), https://doi.org/10.1093/rfs/hhx019; acquisitive firms underperform: Cooper, Gulen & Schill, "Asset Growth and the Cross-Section of Stock Returns" (JF 2008), https://doi.org/10.1111/j.1540-6261.2008.01370.x
# Note: signs were chosen from the first sweep run (field sweep batch 1), so this is partly data-selected; each sign was checked to hold out of sample (OOS1) before inclusion.
# Repair: 7 legs (drops inventories and long-term debt, the weakest out of sample). Parent SWC_BS9 IR .063, TVR .029, corr .477 (< .5), OOS1 .108; needs IR > .07.
ta = ts_fill(total_assets)  # total assets, carried forward between reports
cl = cs_zscore(cs_rank(ts_fill(current_liabilities)/ta))  # short-term operating liabilities per dollar of assets, ranked and z-scored
cp = cs_zscore(cs_rank(ts_fill(current_portion_of_long_term_debt)/ta))  # debt coming due within a year per dollar of assets, ranked and z-scored
ar = cs_zscore(cs_rank(ts_fill(accounts_receivable_excluding_notes)/ta))  # receivables per dollar of assets, ranked and z-scored
gw = -cs_zscore(cs_rank(ts_fill(goodwill)/ta))  # goodwill from acquisitions (short) per dollar of assets, ranked and z-scored
ca = cs_zscore(cs_rank(ts_fill(current_assets_report)/ta))  # current assets per dollar of assets, ranked and z-scored
ad = cs_zscore(cs_rank(ts_fill(accumulated_depreciation)/ta))  # accumulated depreciation (older asset base) per dollar of assets, ranked and z-scored
oc = cs_zscore(cs_rank(ts_fill(other_current_assets)/ta))  # other current assets per dollar of assets, ranked and z-scored
alpha = at_zero2nan(at_nan2zero(cl) + at_nan2zero(cp) + at_nan2zero(ar) + at_nan2zero(gw) + at_nan2zero(ca) + at_nan2zero(ad) + at_nan2zero(oc))  # equal-weight composite; missing legs count as 0

Each item scaled by total assets is a weak, slow characteristic (daily IR .03-.05 alone, turnover ~.03) whose sign held in-sample and out-of-sample (2017-21); combining several weakly related characteristics diversifies their noise, so the composite should carry a higher IR at the same tiny turnover (the IR/sqrt(turnover) route that qualified T_COMP7). Long firms funded by short-term operating liabilities with receivables/inventory-heavy, older (depreciated) asset bases; short goodwill-heavy (acquisitive) and long-term-debt-heavy firms.
# Source: Green, Hand & Zhang, "The Characteristics that Provide Independent Information about Average U.S. Monthly Stock Returns" (RFS 2017), https://doi.org/10.1093/rfs/hhx019; acquisitive firms underperform: Cooper, Gulen & Schill, "Asset Growth and the Cross-Section of Stock Returns" (JF 2008), https://doi.org/10.1111/j.1540-6261.2008.01370.x
# Note: signs were chosen from the first sweep run (field sweep batch 1), so this is partly data-selected; each sign was checked to hold out of sample (OOS1) before inclusion.
# Repair: 7 legs + low-accruals leg. Parent SWC_BS9 IR .063, TVR .029, corr .477 (< .5), OOS1 .108; needs IR > .07.
# Source (accruals): Sloan, The Accounting Review 1996, https://www.jstor.org/stable/248290
ta = ts_fill(total_assets)  # total assets, carried forward between reports
cl = cs_zscore(cs_rank(ts_fill(current_liabilities)/ta))  # short-term operating liabilities per dollar of assets, ranked and z-scored
cp = cs_zscore(cs_rank(ts_fill(current_portion_of_long_term_debt)/ta))  # debt coming due within a year per dollar of assets, ranked and z-scored
ar = cs_zscore(cs_rank(ts_fill(accounts_receivable_excluding_notes)/ta))  # receivables per dollar of assets, ranked and z-scored
gw = -cs_zscore(cs_rank(ts_fill(goodwill)/ta))  # goodwill from acquisitions (short) per dollar of assets, ranked and z-scored
ca = cs_zscore(cs_rank(ts_fill(current_assets_report)/ta))  # current assets per dollar of assets, ranked and z-scored
ad = cs_zscore(cs_rank(ts_fill(accumulated_depreciation)/ta))  # accumulated depreciation (older asset base) per dollar of assets, ranked and z-scored

alpha = at_zero2nan(at_nan2zero(cl) + at_nan2zero(cp) + at_nan2zero(ar) + at_nan2zero(gw) + at_nan2zero(ca) + at_nan2zero(ad) + at_nan2zero(oc) + at_nan2zero(acc))  # equal-weight composite; missing legs count as 0

# Thesis: High prices that coincide with high volume rank are exhausted. (Alpha #44, adapted) Blended with low accruals, whose returns move against short-term price signals, to raise IR and cut turnover.
# Source: Kakushadze, "101 Formulaic Alphas" (2016), https://arxiv.org/abs/1601.00991; Sloan, The Accounting Review 1996, https://www.jstor.org/stable/248290
# Repair: accrual partner 1.5x. Parent A101_044_S Slow IR .067, TVR .786, irtvr .075, corr .602 to #592314 (bar .091).
r = cs_zscore(-ts_corr_binary(high, cs_rank(volume), 5))  # Alpha #44 signal, z-scored
k = cs_zscore(-cs_rank((ts_fill(net_income) - ts_fill(cash_from_operations))/ts_fill(total_assets)))  # low accruals: earnings backed by cash
alpha = at_zero2nan(at_nan2zero(r) + 1.5*at_nan2zero(k))  # Alpha #44 + accruals at 1.5x

# Thesis: A close near the low on a gap-down open rebounds (delay-0 contrarian). (Alpha #54, adapted)
# Note: Slow re-run requested by Abhinav after a strong Fast screen.
# Source: Kakushadze, "101 Formulaic Alphas" (2016), https://arxiv.org/abs/1601.00991
loc = (low - close)/(low - high - 0.001*close)  # how far the close sits above the low, 0..1
alpha = -loc*(open/close)**5  # long closes near the low, scaled by the open-to-close drop

# Thesis: High prices that coincide with high volume rank are exhausted. (Alpha #44, adapted)
# Note: Slow re-run requested by Abhinav after a strong Fast screen.
# Source: Kakushadze, "101 Formulaic Alphas" (2016), https://arxiv.org/abs/1601.00991
alpha = -ts_corr_binary(high, cs_rank(volume), 5)  # negative 5-day corr of high and volume rank

# Thesis: Persistent co-movement of volume and VWAP ranks marks crowded trades. (Alpha #50, adapted)
# Note: Slow re-run requested by Abhinav after a strong Fast screen.
# Source: Kakushadze, "101 Formulaic Alphas" (2016), https://arxiv.org/abs/1601.00991
c = ts_corr_binary(cs_rank(volume), cs_rank(vwap_last_hour), 5)  # 5-day corr of volume rank and VWAP rank
alpha = -ts_max(cs_rank(c), 5)  # short the most persistent co-movers

# Thesis: A change in where the close sits within the day's range reverts. (Alpha #53, adapted)
# Note: Slow re-run requested by Abhinav after a strong Fast screen.
# Source: Kakushadze, "101 Formulaic Alphas" (2016), https://arxiv.org/abs/1601.00991
pos = ((close - low) - (high - close))/(close - low + 0.001*close)  # close location within the day's range
alpha = -delta(pos, 10)  # fade the 10-day change in close location

# Thesis: A close near the low on a gap-down open rebounds (delay-0 contrarian). (Alpha #54, adapted) Blended with low accruals, whose returns move against short-term reversal, to cut turnover and pool correlation.
# Source: Kakushadze, "101 Formulaic Alphas" (2016), https://arxiv.org/abs/1601.00991; Sloan, The Accounting Review 1996, https://www.jstor.org/stable/248290
# Repair: accrual partner 1.5x. Parent A101_054 Fast IR .111, TVR 1.38, Fast pool corr .993.
loc = (low - close)/(low - high - 0.001*close)  # how far the close sits above the low, 0..1
r = cs_zscore(-loc*(open/close)**5)  # Alpha #54: long closes near the low after a drop
k = cs_zscore(-cs_rank((ts_fill(net_income) - ts_fill(cash_from_operations))/ts_fill(total_assets)))  # low accruals: earnings backed by cash (Sloan 1996), the partner behind 3 of our submissions
alpha = at_zero2nan(at_nan2zero(r) + 1.5*at_nan2zero(k))  # reversal + accruals at 1.5x

# Thesis: A close near the low on a gap-down open rebounds (delay-0 contrarian). (Alpha #54, adapted) Blended with low accruals, whose returns move against short-term reversal, to cut turnover and pool correlation.
# Source: Kakushadze, "101 Formulaic Alphas" (2016), https://arxiv.org/abs/1601.00991; Sloan, The Accounting Review 1996, https://www.jstor.org/stable/248290
# Repair: 5-day smoothing. Parent A101_054 Fast IR .111, TVR 1.38, Fast pool corr .993.
loc = (low - close)/(low - high - 0.001*close)  # how far the close sits above the low, 0..1
r = cs_zscore(ts_mean(-loc*(open/close)**5, 5))  # 5-day average of the Alpha #54 signal (lower turnover)
alpha = r  # smoothed contrarian signal

# Thesis: A close near the low on a gap-down open rebounds (delay-0 contrarian). (Alpha #54, adapted) Blended with low accruals, whose returns move against short-term reversal, to cut turnover and pool correlation.
# Source: Kakushadze, "101 Formulaic Alphas" (2016), https://arxiv.org/abs/1601.00991; Sloan, The Accounting Review 1996, https://www.jstor.org/stable/248290
# Repair: 5-day smoothing + accrual partner 1.5x. Parent A101_054 Fast IR .111, TVR 1.38, Fast pool corr .993.
loc = (low - close)/(low - high - 0.001*close)  # how far the close sits above the low, 0..1

alpha = at_zero2nan(at_nan2zero(r) + 1.5*at_nan2zero(k))  # smoothed reversal + accruals at 1.5x

# Source: Green, Hand & Zhang, "The Characteristics that Provide Independent Information about Average U.S. Monthly Stock Returns" (Review of Financial Studies 2017), https://doi.org/10.1093/rfs/hhx019; Hou, Xue & Zhang, "Replicating Anomalies" (Review of Financial Studies 2020), https://doi.org/10.1093/rfs/hhy131

alpha = cs_rank(n)  # long high, short low (portal industry-neutralises)

n = ts_fill(cost_of_goods_sold_to_fixed_expenses_and_production_and_general)  # cost_of_goods_sold_to_fixed_expenses_and_production_and_general: already a dimensionless ratio, carried forward between reports

n = ts_fill(diluted_eps)/close  # diluted_eps per share divided by price: a yield (dimensionless)

n = ts_fill(dividend_per_share)/close  # dividend_per_share per share divided by price: a yield (dimensionless)
